name: industry-pitch
title: BigOrange {{vars.industryLabel}} pitch
audience: A prospect in one of BigOrange's four industries (MSP, manufacturing, landscaping, home builders).

slides.title: {{vars.coverTitle}}
slides.notes:
Open with their world, not ours. One sentence on why we asked for the meeting, then hand the room the agenda.

[Sources]
{{vars.industryHubUrl}}
[/Sources]

slides.title: {{vars.whoTitle}}

card.title: Guides, not heroes
card.body: Certified StoryBrand Guide. HubSpot Partner. Google Partner. Women-owned, Cincinnati-based, and we show our work.

slides.notes: Name the buyer types we see most. Ask which one they are.

slides.title: {{vars.brokenTitle}}
slides.notes: Each card is a pattern from the vertical brief. Ask which two they recognize.

slides.title: {{vars.journeyTitle}}
slides.notes: Walk one real buyer through the steps. Where does a prospect stall today?

slides.title: Message, findability, proof, follow-up

items.title: Say it so a busy buyer gets it
items.body: One clear message, the customer as the hero, and a next step that feels like help.

items.title: Get found by people and by AI answers
items.body: Technical health first, then pages that answer real questions and can be cited.

items.title: Show the work, with permission
items.body: Approved projects, named reviews, and numbers with a source and a date.

items.title: No lead left sitting
items.body: Routing, useful nurture, and sales feedback so marketing and sales agree on what a good lead is.

slides.notes: This is constant across industries. Keep it to 60 seconds; the vertical slides carry the specifics.

slides.title: {{vars.playsTitle}}
slides.notes: Three to six concrete plays from the vertical brief. Say which one we would start with and why.

slides.title: What we can already show

card.title: A number needs a source and a date
card.body: We only present results we can attribute. Anything estimated stays labeled as an estimate until it is verified. That protects you as much as it protects us.

slides.notes: Only verified proof goes on this slide. If a stat is not verified for this industry, leave it out; do not borrow another client's number.

slides.title: From search to a signed deal, in one chain

items.title: Qualification
items.body: sales says yes or no, and why

data.bar: Search Console  +  analytics  +  verified events  +  CRM source  +  sales feedback

slides.notes: Rankings are a leading signal. We keep the chain intact so reporting survives a sales conversation.

slides.title: Fix the foundation, then release in waves

data.takeaway: Every phase ends with a review and a decision, not a bigger idea list.

slides.notes: Set expectations: the first two weeks are repairs and approvals, not launches.

slides.title: A small team that answers the phone

items.body: Positioning, page plans, and the words on the page.
WordPress production, technical health, schema, analytics and reporting.
Project permissions, review sign-off, and sales feedback so we can prove what worked.

slides.notes: Be explicit about what we need from them. It is the reason most engagements stall.

slides.title: {{vars.investmentTitle}}

card.title: Bounded first engagement
card.body: Confirm scope and access, audit, define the priority page or journey, build, stage privately, review, publish only what is approved, verify the live result.

slides.notes: No public pricing page exists on bigorange.marketing (checked 2026-09-02). Use the proposal figure or a starting-at pointer; never invent a number.

slides.title: Let's start with a working session
slides.notes: Ask for the working session, not the contract. Name the date.
